source.text: Τὸν δὲ ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει προσλαμβάνεσθε, μὴ εἰς διακρίσεις διαλογισμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Now the [one] being weak in the faith receive, not for disputes of opinions.

en.L: Now welcome the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over opinions.
en.B: Welcome anyone whose faith is weak, but not in order to quarrel over their opinions.
en.R: Some believers have weak faith. Make them welcome among you, and do not start arguments with them about what they think.

es.L: Ahora bien, {{plural_you:acojan|acoged}} al que es débil en la fe, no para disputas sobre opiniones.
es.B: {{plural_you:Acojan|Acoged}} a quien tenga una fe débil, pero no para discutir sus opiniones.
es.R: Algunos creyentes tienen una fe débil. {{plural_you:Acójanlos|Acogedlos}} entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no {{plural_you:empiecen|empecéis}} discusiones con ellos sobre lo que piensan.

sw.L: Basi yule aliye dhaifu katika imani mpokeeni, si kwa ajili ya mabishano ya maoni.
sw.B: Mpokeeni mtu yeyote ambaye imani yake ni dhaifu, lakini si kwa lengo la kubishana juu ya maoni yake.
sw.R: Baadhi ya waamini wana imani dhaifu. Wapokeeni kati yenu, wala msianzishe mabishano nao kuhusu mawazo yao.

fr.L: Or accueillez celui qui est faible dans la foi, non pour des disputes d’opinions.
fr.B: Accueillez celui dont la foi est faible, mais pas pour discuter de ses opinions.
fr.R: Certains croyants ont une foi faible. Accueillez-les parmi vous, et ne commencez pas à vous disputer avec eux sur ce qu’ils pensent.

ko.L: 믿음이 약한 사람을 받아들이십시오. 그러나 생각을 두고 논쟁하려고 [받아들이지는] 마십시오.
ko.B: 믿음이 약한 사람을 기꺼이 받아들이십시오. 그러나 그의 생각을 두고 따지려고 받아들여서는 안 됩니다.
ko.R: 믿음이 약한 신자들이 있습니다. 그들을 여러분 가운데 기쁘게 맞아들이십시오. 그리고 그들이 생각하는 것을 두고 그들과 말다툼을 시작하지 마십시오.

vi.L: Hãy tiếp nhận người yếu đức tin, nhưng không phải để tranh cãi về các ý kiến.
vi.B: Hãy tiếp nhận người có đức tin còn yếu, nhưng đừng để rồi tranh cãi về những quan điểm của họ.
vi.R: Có những tín hữu đức tin còn yếu. Hãy đón tiếp họ vào giữa anh chị em, và đừng bắt đầu tranh cãi với họ về những điều họ nghĩ.

pt.L: Ora, acolham aquele que é fraco na fé, não para disputas sobre opiniões.
pt.B: Acolham quem tem a fé fraca, mas não para discutir as opiniões dessa pessoa.
pt.R: Algumas pessoas que creem ainda têm a fé fraca. Acolham essas pessoas no meio de vocês e não comecem discussões com elas sobre o que pensam.

decisions.choice: weak in faith: not yet confident before God that one is free in matters such as food and special days
alternatives: weak in trust in God in general
decisions.reason: The chapter shows what Paul means: the weak eat only vegetables (verse 2) and set some days apart (verse 5). Faith here is the settled conviction before God that a thing is allowed (verses 22-23). It is not a verdict on their standing with God, for God has welcomed them (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the weak were most likely keeping Jewish food laws and holy days
alternatives: ascetic avoidance of meat and wine from outside Judaism
fear of meat that had been offered to idols (as in 1 Corinthians 8)
decisions.reason: Paul calls food "unclean" with κοινός (verse 14), the word of Jewish purity law (Mark 7:2; Acts 10:14), and he ends the argument by speaking of Jews and Gentiles together (15:7-12). But he never names the group, and avoiding meat and wine was not itself required by the law, so the exact background is uncertain.
διάκρισις is a deciding between views, here a quarrel; διαλογισμός is a person's thoughts or reasonings. Welcome them, but not so as to argue down their views.

προσλαμβάνομαι is to take someone into your company and fellowship. The same verb says that God has welcomed the person (verse 3) and that the Messiah welcomed you (15:7), so it is "welcome" each time.

decisions.choice: whose faith is weak; some believers
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the one who is weak in faith", a type of person. Balanced and Readable say "anyone" or "some believers" so that the sentence reads naturally.

As throughout Romans (see 1:1), each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros. In this chapter Paul also speaks to one person with "tú" (verses 4, 10, 15, 20-22), which has no setting.

"Recibir" can mean merely to receive a visitor; "acoger" is to take someone in warmly, which is what the verb means. Spanish uses "acoger" here and in verse 3, where God has welcomed the person, as the English uses "welcome" for both.
"Kukaribisha" is to invite a guest in; "kupokea" is to take someone in as one of your own, which is the sense here. The same verb says in verse 3 that God has welcomed ("amempokea") the person.

decisions.choice: celui qui ... il, l’un ... l’autre, with no gender span (for this chapter)
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: The English needs "they" or "he" for the weak and the strong throughout this chapter. French "celui qui", "l’un", "quelqu’un", "chacun" and the "il" that refers back to them are already generic, so, as the French style guide says, no span is added; spans stay on nouns French has to choose, such as "ton frère ou ta sœur".

decisions.choice: the exhortations of chapters 14-15 in 합쇼체 ("-십시오") with "여러분", as through the letter; "받아들이다" (L, B), "맞아들이다" (R) for welcome, here and at 14:3 and 15:7
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:1 and 12:1. The verb means to welcome someone into fellowship (meaning decision at 15:7); "받아들이다" says that without the older church word "용납하다", which now sounds like putting up with someone.

decisions.choice: "믿음이 약한 사람" at every level; "강한 사람" for the strong at 15:1
decisions.reason: "믿음" is the letter's word for faith at every level (1:17); the weakness is in faith, not in body, so Korean names the faith.

decisions.choice: "tiếp nhận" (L, B); "đón tiếp" (R) for this verb (also 14:3 and 15:7)
decisions.reason: The verb is to take someone into one's company and fellowship. "Tiếp nhận" says that a person is received as one of the group; "chấp nhận" would sound like merely tolerating them, and "tiếp đãi" is entertaining a guest. Readable uses the everyday "đón tiếp" (to welcome).

decisions.choice: "tín hữu" (R) for the believers the weak and strong are
decisions.reason: Readable names the weak as believers, as the English Readable does; "tín hữu" is the plain word for a fellow believer, used in the Vietnamese Colossians at Readable (4:13, 4:15), and returns in this chapter where the English Readable says "a fellow believer".

For the whole book (14:1, 14:3; 15:7). "Acolher" is to take someone warmly into one's company, which is what the verb means here; "receber" can sound like merely letting someone in, and "aceitar" like putting up with them. The same word serves for God's welcome (14:3) and the Messiah's (15:7), as the English keeps "welcome".

source.text: ὃς μὲν πιστεύει φαγεῖν πάντα, ὁ δὲ ἀσθενῶν λάχανα ἐσθίει.

records.literal_gloss: One indeed believes to eat all things, but the [one] being weak eats vegetables.

en.L: One person believes [he may] eat all things, but the one who is weak eats vegetables.
en.B: One person believes it is right to eat anything, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.
en.R: One person believes it is all right to eat any kind of food. Another person, whose faith is weak, eats only vegetables.

es.L: Uno cree [que puede] comer de todo, pero el que es débil come verduras.
es.B: Uno cree que puede comer de todo; el débil, en cambio, come solo verduras.
es.R: Hay quien cree que está bien comer cualquier clase de comida. Otro, que tiene una fe débil, solo come verduras.

sw.L: Mtu mmoja anaamini kwamba [anaweza] kula kila kitu, lakini yule aliye dhaifu anakula mboga za majani.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja anaamini kwamba ni halali kula chochote, lakini mwingine, aliye dhaifu, anakula mboga za majani tu.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja anaamini kwamba ni sawa kula chakula cha aina yoyote. Mwingine, ambaye imani yake ni dhaifu, anakula mboga za majani tu.

fr.L: L’un croit [pouvoir] manger de tout, mais celui qui est faible mange des légumes.
fr.B: L’un croit qu’il peut manger de tout, tandis qu’un autre, qui est faible, ne mange que des légumes.
fr.R: Quelqu’un croit qu’il a le droit de manger de toutes sortes d’aliments. Un autre, dont la foi est faible, ne mange que des légumes.

ko.L: 어떤 사람은 모든 것을 먹어도 된다고 믿지만, 약한 사람은 채소를 먹습니다.
ko.B: 어떤 사람은 무엇이든 먹어도 된다고 믿습니다. 그러나 믿음이 약한 사람은 채소만 먹습니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람은 어떤 음식이든 먹어도 괜찮다고 믿습니다. 그러나 믿음이 약한 다른 사람은 채소만 먹습니다.

vi.L: Người này tin rằng [mình được] ăn mọi thứ, còn người yếu thì ăn rau.
vi.B: Có người tin rằng mình được phép ăn mọi thứ, còn người khác, là người yếu, thì chỉ ăn rau.
vi.R: Có người tin rằng mình được ăn mọi loại thức ăn. Còn người có đức tin yếu thì chỉ ăn rau.

pt.L: Um crê [que pode] comer de tudo, mas o que é fraco come legumes.
pt.B: Uma pessoa crê que pode comer de tudo, enquanto outra, que é fraca, come apenas legumes.
pt.R: Uma pessoa acredita que pode comer qualquer tipo de comida. Outra pessoa, que tem a fé fraca, come só legumes.

decisions.choice: believes: has the conviction before God that eating anything is allowed
decisions.reason: πιστεύω with "to eat" is the confidence that a thing is permitted. It is the verb of the noun "faith" in verses 1, 22 and 23, and the strong person's freedom comes from that faith.

decisions.choice: the weak person avoids meat altogether
decisions.reason: Eating vegetables is set against eating everything, so it means eating no meat (verse 21 names meat and wine). Paul does not say why. Jews living among Gentiles sometimes kept off meat that could not be known to be clean, as Daniel and his friends did (Daniel 1:8-16).
The contrast with "anything" shows that the weak eat vegetables and nothing else; Balanced and Readable add "only" to make that plain.

decisions.choice: it is right / it is all right
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "he may" in brackets. Balanced and Readable say "it is right" or "it is all right", which needs no pronoun for a person who may be a man or a woman.

In everyday Swahili "mboga" is any dish eaten with the staple, and it can be a stew of meat or fish. Paul's point is that the weak person eats no meat, so every level says "mboga za majani" (green vegetables).

decisions.choice: "믿음이 약한 사람" (B, R) for "the weak one"
decisions.reason: Korean "약한 사람" alone would suggest a person weak in body or will; Balanced and Readable repeat "믿음이" from verse 1, as the English Readable does.
In Brazil "legumes" is the everyday word for vegetables as food in general; "verduras" are only leafy greens, and "vegetais" sounds technical (it also means plants).

source.text: ὁ ἐσθίων τὸν μὴ ἐσθίοντα μὴ ἐξουθενείτω, ὁ δὲ μὴ ἐσθίων τὸν ἐσθίοντα μὴ κρινέτω, ὁ θεὸς γὰρ αὐτὸν προσελάβετο.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] eating the [one] not eating let not despise, and the [one] not eating the [one] eating let not judge, for the God him received.

en.L: The one who eats must not look down on the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats, for God has welcomed {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: The one who eats must not look down on the one who abstains, and the one who abstains must not pass judgment on the one who eats, because God has welcomed that person.
en.R: If you eat meat, do not look down on people who do not. If you do not eat meat, do not judge people who do. God has welcomed them.

es.L: El que come no debe despreciar al que no come, y el que no come no debe juzgar al que come, porque Dios lo ha acogido.
es.B: El que come no debe mirar con desprecio al que se abstiene, y el que se abstiene no debe juzgar al que come, porque Dios ha acogido a esa persona.
es.R: Si tú comes carne, no desprecies a los que no la comen. Si no comes carne, no juzgues a los que la comen. Dios los ha acogido.

sw.L: Anayekula asimdharau asiyekula, na asiyekula asimhukumu anayekula, kwa maana Mungu amempokea.
sw.B: Anayekula asimdharau yule anayejizuia, na anayejizuia asimhukumu yule anayekula, kwa sababu Mungu amempokea mtu huyo.
sw.R: Kama wewe unakula nyama, usiwadharau wale wasiokula. Kama huli nyama, usiwahukumu wale wanaokula. Mungu amewapokea.

fr.L: Que celui qui mange ne méprise pas celui qui ne mange pas, et que celui qui ne mange pas ne juge pas celui qui mange, car Dieu l’a accueilli.
fr.B: Celui qui mange ne doit pas mépriser celui qui s’abstient, et celui qui s’abstient ne doit pas juger celui qui mange, car Dieu l’a accueilli.
fr.R: Si tu manges de la viande, ne méprise pas ceux qui n’en mangent pas. Si tu ne manges pas de viande, ne juge pas ceux qui en mangent. Dieu les a accueillis.

ko.L: 먹는 사람은 먹지 않는 사람을 업신여기지 말고, 먹지 않는 사람은 먹는 사람을 판단하지 마십시오. 하나님께서 그를 받아들이셨기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 먹는 사람은 먹지 않는 사람을 업신여기지 마십시오. 또 먹지 않는 사람은 먹는 사람을 판단하지 마십시오. 하나님께서 그 사람을 받아들이셨기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 고기를 먹는 사람은 고기를 먹지 않는 사람을 깔보지 마십시오. 고기를 먹지 않는 사람은 고기를 먹는 사람을 판단하지 마십시오. 하나님께서 그들을 받아들이셨습니다.

vi.L: Người ăn đừng khinh người không ăn, và người không ăn đừng xét đoán người ăn, vì Đức Chúa Trời đã tiếp nhận người ấy.
vi.B: Người ăn đừng coi thường người kiêng cữ, và người kiêng cữ đừng xét đoán người ăn, vì Đức Chúa Trời đã tiếp nhận người ấy.
vi.R: Nếu bạn ăn thịt, đừng coi thường những người không ăn. Nếu bạn không ăn thịt, đừng xét đoán những người ăn. Đức Chúa Trời đã tiếp nhận họ.

pt.L: Quem come não despreze quem não come, e quem não come não julgue quem come, pois Deus o acolheu.
pt.B: Quem come não deve desprezar quem se abstém, e quem se abstém não deve julgar quem come, porque Deus acolheu essa pessoa.
pt.R: Se você come carne, não despreze quem não come. Se você não come carne, não julgue quem come. Deus acolheu essas pessoas.

decisions.choice: look down on / judge: the typical fault of each side
decisions.reason: The strong are tempted to despise (ἐξουθενέω) the weak as narrow; the weak are tempted to judge (κρίνω), that is, condemn, the strong as sinners. Paul forbids both, and asks the same two questions again in verse 10.

alternatives: both the eater and the abstainer
decisions.reason: The pronoun follows "the one who eats", the person the abstainer condemns, and God's welcome answers that condemnation. Paul says elsewhere that both are welcomed (15:7), but this sentence speaks of the eater.
Balanced says "abstains" for "does not eat", which is clear in context and avoids repeating "eat" four times.
The Greek says only "eat" and "not eat". Verse 2 and verse 21 show that the food in question is meat, so Readable names it.

decisions.choice: lo, su, sí mismo: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Where the English Literal has a gender span on "him" or "himself" for a person who may be a man or a woman (here and in verses 4, 5, 7, 12, 22 and 23), Spanish uses "lo", "su" and "sí mismo", the ordinary forms for anyone, or needs no pronoun at all, so there is no span. "Él o ella" would add words the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: "업신여기다" (L, B); "깔보다" (R) for look down on; "판단하다" at every level for judge, as settled at 2:1
decisions.reason: Each side's typical fault (meaning decision): the one who eats despises, the one who abstains judges. "판단하다" is the letter's word for people judging others; God's judgment is "심판" (verse 10).
The Korean pronoun does not mark a man or a woman, so the English gender span has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: "khinh" (L), "coi thường" (B, R) and "xét đoán" at every level, kept through the chapter (14:10, 14:13)
decisions.reason: The two verbs name the typical fault of each side (m1): the strong look down, the weak pass judgment. Each keeps one Vietnamese word wherever Paul repeats it, so the reader can follow the two faults through verses 10 and 13.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" (L, B), "họ" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người ấy" and "họ" do not mark sex, so the English gender span has nothing to choose between, here and for the pronouns of this chapter (14:4, 14:6, 14:7, 14:12, 14:22, 14:23); the reflexive "mình" likewise.

The English needs a gender setting for "them/him" here and in the general statements of verses 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 22 and 23. In Portuguese the pronoun refers back to "quem come", "cada um" or "servo", and "o", "si mesmo", "seu" after such words are ordinary generic Portuguese (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7); the subject pronoun is usually dropped. So no setting is used for them in this chapter.

source.text: σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ κρίνων ἀλλότριον οἰκέτην;

records.literal_gloss: You, who are you, the [one] judging another's household servant?

en.L: Who are you, the one who judges another's household servant?
en.B: Who are you to judge someone else's servant?
en.R: Who are you to judge a servant who belongs to someone else?

es.L: ¿Quién eres tú, que juzgas al criado ajeno?
es.B: ¿Quién eres tú para juzgar al criado de otro?
es.R: ¿Quién eres tú para juzgar a un criado que pertenece a otra persona?

sw.L: Wewe ni nani, unayemhukumu mtumishi wa nyumbani wa mwingine?
sw.B: Wewe ni nani hata umhukumu mtumishi wa nyumbani wa mtu mwingine?
sw.R: Wewe ni nani hata umhukumu mtumishi wa nyumbani ambaye ni wa mtu mwingine?

fr.L: Toi, qui es-tu, toi qui juges le domestique d’autrui ?
fr.B: Qui es-tu pour juger le domestique d’un autre ?
fr.R: Qui es-tu pour juger un serviteur qui travaille pour quelqu’un d’autre ?

ko.L: 남의 집 하인을 판단하는 당신은 누구입니까?
ko.B: 당신이 누구이기에 남의 하인을 판단합니까?
ko.R: 다른 사람에게 속한 하인을 판단하다니, 당신은 누구입니까?

vi.L: Bạn là ai mà xét đoán gia nhân của người khác?
vi.B: Bạn là ai mà xét đoán đầy tớ của người khác?
vi.R: Bạn là ai mà xét đoán một người đầy tớ thuộc về người khác?

pt.L: Você, quem é você, que julga o servo doméstico de outro?
pt.B: Quem é você para julgar o servo de outra pessoa?
pt.R: Quem é você para julgar um servo que pertence a outra pessoa?

decisions.reason: οἰκέτης is a servant of a household, usually a slave. The word stresses whose household the servant belongs to, which is Paul's point: the servant answers to the master, not to you.
Nobody had the right to discipline another person's servant. The believer you are judging belongs to the Lord, as the next sentence and verses 7-9 say.
The project says "slave" for the usual word for a slave (1:1), but this is a different word, chosen for the household picture; "servant" keeps the two words apart.

"Esclavo" is kept for the usual word for a slave and "servidor" for the word for one who serves; this is a third word, a servant of a household. "Criado" is a household servant, so it keeps the picture and the three words apart.

"Mtumwa" is kept for the usual word for a slave and "mtumishi" for the word for one who serves. This word is a servant of a household, so Swahili says "mtumishi wa nyumbani" at every level, which keeps the household picture and the words apart.
The word is a household servant (meaning decision), not the usual word for slave; French "domestique" names exactly that. Readable says "serviteur", the plainer word.

decisions.choice: "당신" with 합쇼체 for the singular "you" in this chapter (verses 4, 10, 15, 20-22), as at 2:1, 8:2 and 11:17
decisions.reason: Paul turns to an imagined single reader, as earlier in the letter; "당신" keeps the letter's polite level while showing that one person is addressed.

decisions.choice: "하인" at every level for the household servant
decisions.reason: This word is a servant of a household, not the letter's word for a slave, which Korean renders "종" (1:1); "하인" keeps the picture of someone who answers to his own master (meaning decision).
Paul turns to one imagined reader (m1 of 14:10). As in 2:1 and 8:2, the singular hearer is "bạn"; "anh chị em" stays the plural "you" (14:16).

The word is a household servant (m1), not the usual word for slave. "Gia nhân" is a servant of a house, which keeps the household picture at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "đầy tớ", as the English says "servant".
Paul turns from the church ("vocês", verse 1) to an imagined single reader, as the Greek singular shows, so Portuguese says "você" here and in verses 10, 15 and 20-22.
This is not the usual word for a slave ("escravo" at Literal elsewhere) but the word for a servant of a household; Literal adds "doméstico" to keep the household picture the meaning note stresses.

source.text: τῷ ἰδίῳ κυρίῳ στήκει ἢ πίπτει· σταθήσεται δέ, δυνατεῖ γὰρ ὁ κύριος στῆσαι αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: To the own master he stands or falls; but he will be made to stand, for able is the Lord to make stand him.

en.L: To {{gender:their|his}} own master {{gender:they stand|he stands}} or {{gender:fall|falls}}; and {{gender:they|he}} will be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make {{gender:them|him}} stand.
en.B: It is to their own master that they stand or fall. And they will stand, because the Lord has the power to keep them standing.
en.R: Whether that servant does well or fails is up to the master, not you. And the servant will stand firm, because the Lord is able to hold them up.

es.L: Para su propio señor está en pie o cae; y será sostenido en pie, porque el Señor es capaz de sostenerlo en pie.
es.B: Es ante su propio señor como se mantiene en pie o cae. Y se mantendrá en pie, porque el Señor tiene poder para sostenerlo.
es.R: Si a ese criado le va bien o le va mal, eso es asunto de su señor, no tuyo. Y el criado se mantendrá firme, porque el Señor puede sostenerlo.

sw.L: Kwa bwana wake mwenyewe yeye anasimama au anaanguka; lakini atawezeshwa kusimama, kwa maana Bwana ana uwezo wa kumsimamisha.
sw.B: Ni mbele ya bwana wake mwenyewe kwamba anasimama au anaanguka. Naye atasimama, kwa sababu Bwana ana uwezo wa kumshikilia asimame.
sw.R: Kama mtumishi huyo anafanya vizuri au anashindwa, hilo ni jambo la bwana wake, si lako. Na mtumishi huyo atasimama imara, kwa sababu Bwana anaweza kumshikilia.

fr.L: Pour son propre maître il se tient debout ou il tombe ; et il sera tenu debout, car le Seigneur a le pouvoir de le faire tenir debout.
fr.B: C’est devant son propre maître qu’il tient bon ou qu’il tombe. Et il tiendra bon, car le Seigneur a le pouvoir de le garder debout.
fr.R: Que ce serviteur réussisse ou échoue, cela regarde son maître, pas toi. Et il restera debout, car le Seigneur est capable de le soutenir.

ko.L: 그가 서 있든지 넘어지든지 그것은 자기 주인에게 [달린 일]입니다. 그러나 그는 세워질 것입니다. 주님께서 그를 세우실 능력이 있으시기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그가 서든지 넘어지든지, 그것은 그의 주인이 판단할 일입니다. 그리고 그는 서 있게 될 것입니다. 주님께서 그를 서 있게 하실 수 있기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그 하인이 일을 잘하든지 잘못하든지, 그것은 당신이 아니라 그의 주인이 정할 일입니다. 그리고 그 하인은 굳게 설 것입니다. 주님께서 그를 붙들어 주실 수 있기 때문입니다.

vi.L: Người ấy đứng hay ngã là đối với chủ của chính mình; nhưng người ấy sẽ được đứng vững, vì Chúa có quyền làm cho người ấy đứng vững.
vi.B: Người ấy đứng hay ngã là việc của chủ mình. Và người ấy sẽ đứng vững, vì Chúa có quyền năng giữ cho người ấy đứng vững.
vi.R: Người đầy tớ ấy làm tốt hay thất bại là do chủ của họ xét, chứ không phải bạn. Và người ấy sẽ đứng vững, vì Chúa có thể giữ cho họ đứng vững.

pt.L: Para o seu próprio senhor ele fica de pé ou cai; mas será mantido de pé, pois o Senhor é poderoso para mantê-lo de pé.
pt.B: É diante do seu próprio senhor que ele fica de pé ou cai. E ficará de pé, porque o Senhor tem poder para sustentá-lo.
pt.R: Se esse servo vai bem ou fracassa, quem decide é o senhor dele, não você. E o servo vai ficar firme, porque o Senhor é capaz de sustentá-lo.

decisions.choice: master, then Lord: the picture turns to Christ
decisions.reason: κύριος means the owner of a servant and also "the Lord". Paul begins with the household picture and ends by speaking of the Lord himself, who is Christ, Lord of the dead and the living (verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: stands or falls: is approved or not; will be made to stand: will be upheld
alternatives: is acquitted or condemned at the last judgment
decisions.reason: Standing and falling is the servant's standing in the master's eyes. The passive "will be made to stand", with the Lord's power as the reason, says that the Lord will keep this believer standing; judgment comes in verse 10.
Some later manuscripts read "God" (θεός) here instead of "the Lord". The SBLGNT follows the earliest manuscripts. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: they / their / them for the servant
decisions.reason: The servant stands for any believer, man or woman. Balanced and Readable use "they" for one person; Literal keeps "he" as a gender setting.

decisions.choice: is up to the master, not you
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain the point of "to their own master": the servant answers to the master, not to the one judging.

Spanish "señor" is both the master of a servant and "the Lord", as the Greek word is, so the sentence can move from the household picture to Christ with the same word, written lowercase and then with a capital. "Amo" would lose the link.
Swahili "bwana" is both the master of a servant and "the Lord", as the Greek word is, so the sentence moves from the household picture to Christ with one word, lowercase and then with a capital.

The Greek uses one word for both; the picture turns from the servant's master to Christ (meaning decision). French says "maître" for the master of a household and "Seigneur" for the Lord, as the English says "master" and "Lord".

decisions.choice: "주인" for the master, then "주님" with the honorific for the Lord
decisions.reason: The picture turns from a household master to Christ (meaning decision); Korean shows the turn with "주님" and the honorific "세우실", since one word cannot do both jobs here.

decisions.choice: "그" for the servant, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "그" does not say whether the servant is a man or a woman, so no setting is needed.
One Greek word means both master and Lord, and the picture turns from the servant's master to Christ (m1). Vietnamese, like English, needs two words, as the Vietnamese Colossians does (3:22, 4:1).

source.text: Ὃς μὲν κρίνει ἡμέραν παρ’ ἡμέραν, ὃς δὲ κρίνει πᾶσαν ἡμέραν· ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ πληροφορείσθω·

records.literal_gloss: One indeed judges a day beyond a day, but another judges every day; each in the own mind let be fully convinced;

en.L: One person judges one day above another day, but another judges every day [alike]; let each be fully convinced in {{gender:their|his}} own mind;
en.B: One person regards one day as more important than another, while someone else regards every day as the same. Each person must be fully convinced in their own mind.
en.R: Some people think one day is more special than the others. Other people think every day is the same. Each person should be sure in their own mind about what is right.

es.L: Uno juzga un día por encima de [otro] día, pero otro juzga todo día [igual]; cada uno esté plenamente convencido en su propia mente;
es.B: Uno estima un día por encima de otro, mientras que otro estima que todos los días son iguales. Cada cual debe estar plenamente convencido en su propia mente.
es.R: Algunas personas piensan que un día es más especial que los demás. Otras piensan que todos los días son iguales. Cada uno debe estar seguro en su propia mente de lo que es correcto.

sw.L: Mtu mmoja anahukumu siku moja kuwa juu ya siku [nyingine], lakini mwingine anahukumu kila siku [kuwa sawa]; kila mmoja na asadiki kikamilifu akilini mwake mwenyewe;
sw.B: Mtu mmoja anaiona siku fulani kuwa muhimu kuliko nyingine, na mwingine anaziona siku zote kuwa sawa. Kila mtu anapaswa kusadiki kabisa akilini mwake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Watu wengine wanafikiri siku moja ni maalum kuliko nyingine. Wengine wanafikiri siku zote ni sawa. Kila mtu anapaswa kuwa na uhakika moyoni mwake kuhusu lililo sawa.

fr.L: L’un juge un jour au-dessus d’un [autre] jour, l’autre juge tous les jours [égaux] ; que chacun soit pleinement convaincu dans sa propre pensée ;
fr.B: L’un estime qu’un jour est plus important qu’un autre, tandis qu’un autre estime que tous les jours se valent. Chacun doit être pleinement convaincu dans sa propre pensée.
fr.R: Certains pensent qu’un jour est plus spécial que les autres. D’autres pensent que tous les jours sont pareils. Chacun doit être bien sûr, dans son esprit, de ce qui est juste.

ko.L: 어떤 사람은 [어떤] 날을 다른 날보다 [중요하게] 여기고, 어떤 사람은 모든 날을 [같게] 여깁니다. 각 사람은 자기 마음에 확신을 가지십시오.
ko.B: 어떤 사람은 어느 한 날을 다른 날보다 더 중요하게 여기고, 또 어떤 사람은 모든 날을 똑같이 여깁니다. 각자 자기 마음에 확신을 가져야 합니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람들은 어느 한 날이 다른 날보다 더 특별하다고 생각합니다. 다른 사람들은 모든 날이 똑같다고 생각합니다. 각 사람은 무엇이 옳은지 자기 마음속으로 확실히 알고 있어야 합니다.

vi.L: Người này xét ngày này trọng hơn ngày kia, còn người kia xét mọi ngày [đều như nhau]; mỗi người hãy hoàn toàn tin chắc trong tâm trí mình;
vi.B: Có người coi ngày này quan trọng hơn ngày khác, còn người khác coi mọi ngày đều như nhau. Mỗi người phải hoàn toàn tin chắc trong tâm trí mình.
vi.R: Có người nghĩ rằng một ngày nào đó đặc biệt hơn những ngày khác. Có người lại nghĩ mọi ngày đều như nhau. Mỗi người nên tự mình chắc chắn về điều gì là đúng.

pt.L: Um julga um dia acima de [outro] dia, e outro julga todos os dias [iguais]; cada um esteja plenamente convicto em sua própria mente;
pt.B: Uma pessoa considera um dia mais importante que outro, enquanto outra considera todos os dias iguais. Cada um deve estar plenamente convicto em sua própria mente.
pt.R: Algumas pessoas acham que um dia é mais especial que os outros. Outras acham que todos os dias são iguais. Cada pessoa deve ter plena certeza, no seu íntimo, sobre o que é correto.

decisions.choice: special days: most likely the Sabbath and the Jewish feasts and fasts
decisions.reason: Paul does not name the days. Coming beside food that some call "unclean" (verse 14), the Sabbath and the festivals of the law are the most likely (Galatians 4:10; Colossians 2:16).
κρίνω is the same verb as "judge" in verses 3, 4, 10 and 13. Here it means to rate one day above another; Paul plays on its senses through the chapter.
πληροφορέω is to be fully assured. Each believer should act from a settled conviction before the Lord, which verse 23 calls faith.
Literal keeps "judges" so that the reader can see the same verb as in verses 3, 4, 10 and 13.
Readable says what each person is to be sure of.

Literal keeps "kuhukumu", the verb used for "judge" in verses 3, 4, 10 and 13, so that the reader can see Paul's play on it. Swahili rarely uses "kuhukumu" for rating one thing above another, so Balanced and Readable say "kuona" (to regard).

decisions.choice: "여기다" (L, B); "생각하다" (R) for the verb the English Literal renders "judges"
decisions.reason: The verb here means to consider or rate (meaning decision). Korean "판단하다" would make it the same word as "judging" others in verses 3-4; "여기다" gives this sense.

decisions.choice: "확신을 가지다" (L); "확신을 가져야 하다" (B); "확실히 알고 있어야 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: Fully convinced (meaning decision); the Greek command to each person is said as a third-person instruction in Korean.
The verb is the one rendered "xét đoán" (judge) in 14:3-4, here meaning to consider or rate (m2). Literal keeps "xét" so the reader sees the same root; Balanced and Readable say what it means here.

source.text: ὁ φρονῶν τὴν ἡμέραν κυρίῳ φρονεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] regarding the day to [the] Lord regards [it].

en.L: The one who observes the day observes [it] for [the] Lord.
en.B: Whoever observes the day does so for the Lord.
en.R: People who keep a special day do it to honor the Lord.

es.L: El que guarda el día, para [el] Señor [lo] guarda.
es.B: Quien guarda un día especial lo hace para el Señor.
es.R: Los que guardan un día especial lo hacen para honrar al Señor.

sw.L: Anayeishika siku, anaishika kwa ajili ya Bwana.
sw.B: Anayeishika siku hiyo anafanya hivyo kwa ajili ya Bwana.
sw.R: Watu wanaoshika siku maalum hufanya hivyo ili kumheshimu Bwana.

fr.L: Celui qui observe le jour [l’]observe pour [le] Seigneur.
fr.B: Celui qui observe un jour particulier le fait pour le Seigneur.
fr.R: Ceux qui respectent un jour spécial le font pour honorer le Seigneur.

ko.L: 날을 중히 여기는 사람은 주님을 위하여 중히 여깁니다.
ko.B: 어떤 날을 지키는 사람은 주님을 위해 그렇게 합니다.
ko.R: 특별한 날을 지키는 사람은 주님을 높이려고 그렇게 합니다.

vi.L: Người giữ ngày [ấy] thì giữ vì Chúa.
vi.B: Ai giữ ngày ấy là giữ vì Chúa.
vi.R: Người giữ một ngày đặc biệt là làm vậy để tôn kính Chúa.

pt.L: Quem observa o dia o observa para [o] Senhor.
pt.B: Quem guarda o dia faz isso para o Senhor.
pt.R: Quem guarda um dia especial faz isso para honrar o Senhor.

decisions.choice: for the Lord: in the Lord's honor and service
decisions.reason: The dative says for whom the day is kept. Both sides act as servants of the same Lord (verse 4), so neither may condemn the other.

alternatives: later manuscripts add "and the one who does not observe the day does not observe it for the Lord"
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts do not have the added clause, which fills out the pattern of the sentences about eating. It is in many later manuscripts and in the printed Greek editions of the sixteenth century. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)
Readable says what "for the Lord" means.

decisions.choice: "주님을 위하여" (L); "주님을 위해" (B); "주님을 높이려고" (R), here and through verse 8
decisions.reason: In the Lord's honor and service (meaning decision). "주님" with the honorific for the Lord, at every level, as through the letter outside quotations.

decisions.choice: "vì Chúa" (L, B) for "to the Lord" (also 14:6, 14:8: "cho Chúa")
decisions.reason: The dative means in the Lord's honor and service (m1). "Vì Chúa" (for the Lord's sake) says that; in 14:7-8, where Paul sets living "to oneself" against living "to the Lord", Vietnamese says "sống cho", which keeps the contrast.

source.text: καὶ ὁ ἐσθίων κυρίῳ ἐσθίει, εὐχαριστεῖ γὰρ τῷ θεῷ· καὶ ὁ μὴ ἐσθίων κυρίῳ οὐκ ἐσθίει, καὶ εὐχαριστεῖ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] eating to [the] Lord eats, for he gives thanks to the God; and the [one] not eating to [the] Lord not eats, and gives thanks to the God.

en.L: And the one who eats, eats for [the] Lord, for {{gender:they give|he gives}} thanks to God; and the one who does not eat, for [the] Lord does not eat, and gives thanks to God.
en.B: Those who eat do so for the Lord, since they give thanks to God; and those who abstain do so for the Lord, and they too give thanks to God.
en.R: People who eat meat do it to honor the Lord, because they thank God for their food. People who do not eat meat also do it to honor the Lord, and they thank God too.

es.L: Y el que come, para [el] Señor come, porque da gracias a Dios; y el que no come, para [el] Señor no come, y da gracias a Dios.
es.B: Los que comen lo hacen para el Señor, pues dan gracias a Dios; y los que se abstienen lo hacen para el Señor, y también dan gracias a Dios.
es.R: Los que comen carne lo hacen para honrar al Señor, porque dan gracias a Dios por su comida. Los que no comen carne también lo hacen para honrar al Señor, y también dan gracias a Dios.

sw.L: Na anayekula, anakula kwa ajili ya Bwana, kwa maana anamshukuru Mungu; na asiyekula, kwa ajili ya Bwana hali, naye anamshukuru Mungu.
sw.B: Wanaokula hufanya hivyo kwa ajili ya Bwana, kwa kuwa wanamshukuru Mungu; na wanaojizuia hufanya hivyo kwa ajili ya Bwana, nao pia wanamshukuru Mungu.
sw.R: Watu wanaokula nyama hufanya hivyo ili kumheshimu Bwana, kwa sababu wanamshukuru Mungu kwa chakula chao. Watu wasiokula nyama pia hufanya hivyo ili kumheshimu Bwana, nao wanamshukuru Mungu pia.

fr.L: Et celui qui mange, mange pour [le] Seigneur, car il rend grâce à Dieu ; et celui qui ne mange pas, c’est pour [le] Seigneur qu’il ne mange pas, et il rend grâce à Dieu.
fr.B: Ceux qui mangent le font pour le Seigneur, puisqu’ils rendent grâce à Dieu ; et ceux qui s’abstiennent le font pour le Seigneur, et eux aussi rendent grâce à Dieu.
fr.R: Ceux qui mangent de la viande le font pour honorer le Seigneur, car ils remercient Dieu pour leur nourriture. Ceux qui n’en mangent pas le font aussi pour honorer le Seigneur, et eux aussi remercient Dieu.

ko.L: 그리고 먹는 사람도 주님을 위하여 먹습니다. 하나님께 감사하기 때문입니다. 먹지 않는 사람도 주님을 위하여 먹지 않으며, 하나님께 감사합니다.
ko.B: 먹는 사람도 주님을 위해 먹습니다. 그가 하나님께 감사를 드리기 때문입니다. 먹지 않는 사람도 주님을 위해 먹지 않으며, 그 역시 하나님께 감사를 드립니다.
ko.R: 고기를 먹는 사람은 주님을 높이려고 먹습니다. 그는 자기 음식을 두고 하나님께 감사드리기 때문입니다. 고기를 먹지 않는 사람도 주님을 높이려고 먹지 않습니다. 그 사람도 하나님께 감사드립니다.

vi.L: Và người ăn thì ăn vì Chúa, vì người ấy tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời; còn người không ăn thì vì Chúa mà không ăn, và cũng tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Người ăn thì ăn vì Chúa, vì họ tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời; người kiêng cữ thì kiêng vì Chúa, và họ cũng tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Người ăn thịt làm vậy để tôn kính Chúa, vì họ cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về thức ăn của mình. Người không ăn thịt cũng làm vậy để tôn kính Chúa, và họ cũng cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: E quem come, come para [o] Senhor, pois dá graças a Deus; e quem não come, para [o] Senhor não come, e dá graças a Deus.
pt.B: Os que comem fazem isso para o Senhor, já que dão graças a Deus; e os que se abstêm fazem isso para o Senhor, e também eles dão graças a Deus.
pt.R: Quem come carne faz isso para honrar o Senhor, porque agradece a Deus pela comida. Quem não come carne também faz isso para honrar o Senhor, e também agradece a Deus.

decisions.choice: giving thanks: the thanksgiving said over a meal
decisions.reason: Jews and Christians gave thanks to God before eating (1 Corinthians 10:30; 1 Timothy 4:3-5). The one who eats and the one who abstains both thank God, so both are acting before God.
As in the first half of the verse, the dative says for whom each one acts.

decisions.choice: those who eat / those who abstain
alternatives: the one who eats / the one who does not eat
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the general singular into a plural, which reads naturally and needs no "he".
As in verse 3, Readable names the food in question, which verses 2 and 21 show is meat, and says what the thanks is for.
"Rendre grâce" is the French expression for the thanksgiving said to God over a meal (meaning decision); Readable says "remercier", the everyday verb.
As the English Readable does: the meaning decisions say the weak avoid meat and the thanks is said over a meal.

source.text: Οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἑαυτῷ ζῇ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἑαυτῷ ἀποθνῄσκει·

records.literal_gloss: For no one of us to himself lives, and no one to himself dies;

en.L: For none of us lives to {{gender:themselves|himself}}, and no one dies to {{gender:themselves|himself}};
en.B: For not one of us lives for ourselves, and not one of us dies for ourselves.
en.R: None of us lives only for ourselves, and none of us dies only for ourselves.

es.L: Porque ninguno de nosotros vive para sí mismo, y ninguno muere para sí mismo;
es.B: Porque ninguno de nosotros vive para sí mismo, y ninguno de nosotros muere para sí mismo.
es.R: Ninguno de nosotros vive solo para sí mismo, y ninguno muere solo para sí mismo.

sw.L: Kwa maana hakuna yeyote kati yetu anayeishi kwa ajili ya nafsi yake, na hakuna anayekufa kwa ajili ya nafsi yake;
sw.B: Hakuna hata mmoja wetu anayeishi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe, na hakuna hata mmoja wetu anayekufa kwa ajili yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Hakuna hata mmoja wetu anayeishi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe tu, na hakuna anayekufa kwa ajili yake mwenyewe tu.

fr.L: Car aucun de nous ne vit pour lui-même, et aucun ne meurt pour lui-même ;
fr.B: Car aucun de nous ne vit pour soi-même, et aucun de nous ne meurt pour soi-même.
fr.R: Aucun de nous ne vit seulement pour lui-même, et aucun de nous ne meurt seulement pour lui-même.

ko.L: 우리 가운데 아무도 자기 자신을 위하여 살지 않고, 아무도 자기 자신을 위하여 죽지 않습니다.
ko.B: 우리 가운데 누구도 자기만을 위해 살지 않고, 누구도 자기만을 위해 죽지 않습니다.
ko.R: 우리 가운데 아무도 자기 자신만을 위해 살지 않습니다. 또 아무도 자기 자신만을 위해 죽지 않습니다.

vi.L: Vì không ai trong chúng ta sống cho chính mình, và không ai chết cho chính mình;
vi.B: Vì không một ai trong chúng ta sống cho riêng mình, cũng không ai chết cho riêng mình.
vi.R: Không ai trong chúng ta sống chỉ cho riêng mình, và không ai chết chỉ cho riêng mình.

pt.L: Pois nenhum de nós vive para si mesmo, e nenhum morre para si mesmo;
pt.B: Pois nenhum de nós vive para si mesmo, e nenhum de nós morre para si mesmo.
pt.R: Nenhum de nós vive só para si mesmo, e nenhum de nós morre só para si mesmo.

decisions.choice: to oneself: as one's own master
decisions.reason: The contrast in the next verse is "to the Lord". Paul does not mean that people depend on each other, true as that is, but that no believer belongs to themselves: life and death are both lived for the Lord.
Readable adds "only" so that the sentence does not seem to say that believers gain nothing themselves; the point is whom they live for.
Korean "자기" covers men and women alike, so the English gender span has nothing to change.

source.text: ἐάν τε γὰρ ζῶμεν, τῷ κυρίῳ ζῶμεν, ἐάν τε ἀποθνῄσκωμεν, τῷ κυρίῳ ἀποθνῄσκομεν.

records.literal_gloss: For both if we live, to the Lord we live, and if we die, to the Lord we die.

en.L: For if we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord.
en.B: If we live, we live for the Lord; if we die, we die for the Lord.
en.R: If we live, we live for the Lord. If we die, we die for the Lord.

es.L: Porque si vivimos, vivimos para el Señor, y si morimos, morimos para el Señor.
es.B: Si vivimos, vivimos para el Señor; si morimos, morimos para el Señor.
es.R: Si vivimos, es para el Señor. Si morimos, también es para el Señor.

sw.L: Kwa maana tukiishi, tunaishi kwa Bwana, na tukifa, tunakufa kwa Bwana.
sw.B: Tukiishi, tunaishi kwa ajili ya Bwana; tukifa, tunakufa kwa ajili ya Bwana.
sw.R: Tukiishi, ni kwa ajili ya Bwana. Tukifa, pia ni kwa ajili ya Bwana.

fr.B: Si nous vivons, nous vivons pour le Seigneur ; si nous mourons, nous mourons pour le Seigneur.
fr.R: Si nous vivons, c’est pour le Seigneur. Si nous mourons, c’est aussi pour le Seigneur.

ko.L: 우리가 살아도 주님을 위하여 살고, 죽어도 주님을 위하여 죽습니다.
ko.B: 우리는 살아도 주님을 위해 살고, 죽어도 주님을 위해 죽습니다.
ko.R: 우리가 산다면 주님을 위해 삽니다. 우리가 죽는다면 주님을 위해 죽습니다.

vi.L: Vì nếu chúng ta sống, là sống cho Chúa; nếu chúng ta chết, là chết cho Chúa.
vi.B: Nếu chúng ta sống, là sống cho Chúa; nếu chúng ta chết, là chết cho Chúa.
vi.R: Nếu chúng ta sống, chúng ta sống cho Chúa. Nếu chúng ta chết, chúng ta chết cho Chúa.

pt.L: Pois, se vivemos, vivemos para o Senhor, e, se morremos, morremos para o Senhor.
pt.B: Se vivemos, vivemos para o Senhor; se morremos, morremos para o Senhor.
pt.R: Se vivemos, vivemos para o Senhor. Se morremos, morremos para o Senhor.

decisions.choice: to the Lord: for the Lord, as belonging to him
decisions.reason: The dative is the same as in verse 6. Every part of a believer's life, and even death, is for the Lord.
Literal keeps "to the Lord" as in the Greek; Balanced and Readable say "for the Lord", which says plainly what the dative means.
The English Literal keeps "to the Lord". Spanish cannot say "vivir al Señor", so Literal too says "para el Señor", the plain meaning of the dative.

The English Literal keeps "to the Lord" apart from "for the Lord". Portuguese "para o Senhor" covers both the Greek dative and its sense (for, belonging to the Lord), while "vivemos ao Senhor" is not Portuguese; so Literal says "para" too.

source.text: ἐάν τε οὖν ζῶμεν ἐάν τε ἀποθνῄσκωμεν, τοῦ κυρίου ἐσμέν.

records.literal_gloss: If both therefore we live, if also we die, of the Lord we are.

en.L: So whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
en.B: So, living or dying, we belong to the Lord.
en.R: So whether we are alive or dead, we belong to the Lord.

es.L: Así que, sea que vivamos o sea que muramos, del Señor somos.
es.B: Así que, vivos o muertos, pertenecemos al Señor.
es.R: Así que, estemos vivos o muertos, somos del Señor.

sw.L: Basi, kama tunaishi au kama tunakufa, sisi ni wa Bwana.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, tukiwa hai au tukifa, sisi ni wa Bwana.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, tukiwa hai au tukiwa tumekufa, sisi ni watu wa Bwana.

fr.L: Soit donc que nous vivions, soit que nous mourions, nous sommes au Seigneur.
fr.B: Ainsi, vivants ou morts, nous appartenons au Seigneur.
fr.R: Que nous soyons vivants ou morts, nous appartenons donc au Seigneur.

ko.L: 그러므로 우리가 살든지 죽든지 우리는 주님의 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 살든지 죽든지 우리는 주님께 속한 사람들입니다.
ko.R: 그러므로 우리가 살아 있든지 죽었든지, 우리는 주님께 속해 있습니다.

vi.L: Vậy dù chúng ta sống hay dù chúng ta chết, chúng ta là của Chúa.
vi.B: Vậy, dù sống hay chết, chúng ta đều thuộc về Chúa.
vi.R: Vậy dù còn sống hay đã chết, chúng ta vẫn thuộc về Chúa.

pt.L: Assim, quer vivamos, quer morramos, somos do Senhor.
pt.B: Portanto, vivendo ou morrendo, pertencemos ao Senhor.
pt.R: Então, estando vivos ou mortos, pertencemos ao Senhor.

decisions.choice: the Lord's: belonging to the Lord
decisions.reason: The genitive is of ownership, as a servant belongs to a master (verse 4). This is the conclusion of verses 7-8.
Belonging to the Lord (meaning decision); Literal keeps the bare genitive.

source.text: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἔζησεν ἵνα καὶ νεκρῶν καὶ ζώντων κυριεύσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: For to this Christ died and lived, that both of dead and of living he might be lord.

en.L: For to this [end] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died and lived [again], so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might be Lord of both [the] dead and [the] living.
en.B: This is why {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died and came to life: so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be Lord of both the dead and the living.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} died and came back to life for this reason: to be Lord over both the dead and the living.

es.L: Porque para esto {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió y vivió [otra vez]: para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fuera Señor tanto de [los] muertos como de [los] vivos.
es.B: Por esto murió {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} y volvió a la vida: para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fuera Señor de los muertos y de los vivos.
es.R: {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} murió y volvió a la vida por esta razón: para ser Señor de los muertos y de los vivos.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa ajili ya hili {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa na akaishi [tena], ili {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} awe Bwana wa wafu na wa walio hai pia.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa na kurudi kwenye uhai: ili {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawale kama Bwana juu ya wafu na walio hai.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa na akafufuka kwa sababu hii: ili awe Bwana wa wafu na wa walio hai.

fr.L: Car c’est pour cela que {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort et a vécu [de nouveau] : pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit Seigneur et des morts et des vivants.
fr.B: Voici pourquoi le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort et est revenu à la vie : pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit le Seigneur des morts et des vivants.
fr.R: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort et revenu à la vie pour cette raison : pour être le Seigneur des morts et des vivants.

ko.L: 이를 위하여 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죽으셨다가 [다시] 사셨습니다. 그분이 죽은 사람들과 산 사람들의 주님이 되시려는 것입니다.
ko.B: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죽으시고 다시 살아나신 것은 바로 이 때문입니다. 그분은 죽은 사람들과 산 사람들 모두의 주님이 되시려고 그렇게 하셨습니다.
ko.R: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 이 일을 위해 죽으셨다가 다시 살아나셨습니다. 죽은 사람들과 살아 있는 사람들 모두를 다스리시는 주님이 되시려는 것입니다.

vi.L: Vì chính vì điều này mà {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết và sống [lại], để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm Chúa của cả kẻ chết lẫn người sống.
vi.B: Chính vì điều này mà {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết và sống lại: để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm Chúa của cả người chết lẫn người sống.
vi.R: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết và sống lại vì lý do này: để làm Chúa trên cả người chết lẫn người sống.

pt.L: Pois para este [fim] {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} morreu e viveu [de novo], a fim de que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fosse Senhor tanto dos mortos como dos vivos.
pt.B: Foi por isso que {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} morreu e voltou à vida: para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fosse Senhor tanto dos mortos como dos vivos.
pt.R: {{christos:Cristo|O Messias}} morreu e voltou à vida por este motivo: para ser Senhor tanto dos mortos como dos vivos.

decisions.choice: lived: came to life again, his resurrection
decisions.reason: The order is "died and lived", so the living comes after the death: it is the resurrection. Revelation 2:8 uses the same verb in the same way: "who was dead and came to life".
κυριεύω is formed from κύριος, "Lord". Christ's death and resurrection made him Lord of all his people, those who have died and those who are alive, which is why "we are the Lord's" (verse 8).

alternatives: later manuscripts read "died and rose and lived again" or similar
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have two verbs; later ones vary, adding "rose" or changing "lived" to "lived again", to make the reference to the resurrection explicit. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)
The verb is simply "lived", but here it means returning to life after death (m1), which Literal shows with a bracketed "again".

The meaning decision says that "lived" here is the resurrection. Readable says so with the common word "kufufuka" (to rise from the dead), which young readers know; Literal and Balanced keep the verb "to live".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean; "그분" and the honorific -시- for Christ
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (docs/korean-style.md section 7); respect is carried by "께서", "그분" and "-시-" at every level, as through the letter.
"Lived" here means came to life again (meaning decision); Literal brackets "again", as the English Literal does.
This is the verb kept as "làm chủ" in 6:9 and 6:14, where death and sin are the masters. Here Christ rules as Lord (m2), and the verse picks up "the Lord" of verse 8, so Vietnamese says "làm Chúa".

For the whole book. The English Literal writes bare "Messiah" where the Greek has no article, but Portuguese uses "Messias" as a title only with the article ("o Messias morreu"), while "Cristo" stands alone as a name. The article goes inside the alternative so that both options read naturally, as the letters' note asks.

en.B: You, then, why do you pass judgment on your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}?
en.R: You who do not eat meat, why do you judge a fellow believer?

es.B: Y tú, ¿por qué juzgas a tu hermano?
es.R: Tú, que no comes carne, ¿por qué juzgas a otro creyente?

sw.R: Wewe usiyekula nyama, kwa nini unamhukumu mwamini mwenzako?

ko.L: 그런데 당신은 왜 당신의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 판단합니까?
ko.B: 그런데 당신은 왜 당신의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 판단합니까?
ko.R: 고기를 먹지 않는 여러분, 왜 함께 믿는 사람을 판단합니까?

vi.L: Còn bạn, sao bạn xét đoán {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình?
vi.B: Vậy bạn, tại sao bạn xét đoán {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình?

pt.B: E você, então, por que julga o seu {{gender:irmão ou irmã|irmão}}?
pt.R: Você que não come carne, por que julga um irmão ou uma irmã na fé?

decisions.reason: The two questions of this verse answer the two faults of verse 3: the abstainer judges, the eater looks down. This first "you" is the abstainer.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: ἀδελφός is a member of the family of believers.

decisions.choice: You who do not eat meat
decisions.reason: Readable says which person Paul is addressing (m1).

As in Romans 1:13, Spanish "hermano" covers a fellow believer, man or woman, so there is no gender span here or in verses 13, 15 and 21. Readable says "otro creyente", as the English Readable says "a fellow believer".

As in Romans 1:13, "ndugu" already means brother or sister, so Swahili needs no gender span here or in verses 13, 15 and 21. Readable says "mwamini mwenzako" (your fellow believer), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}} (for chapters 14-16)
decisions.reason: The word means a fellow believer, man or woman (meaning decision). French adds the possessive to each noun, so the span covers "ton" as well, and only the noun phrase changes with the setting. Readable says "un autre croyant", as the English Readable says "a fellow believer".

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}}" (L, B) for the singular "brother"; "함께 믿는 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: A fellow believer, man or woman (meaning decision). Korean "형제자매" can name one fellow believer as well as many, so the letter's span is used; Readable says "함께 믿는 사람" (a fellow believer), which needs no setting, as "믿는 사람들" in Colossians 4:15.
The "you" is the one who abstains (meaning decision); Readable names that person as the English Readable does, addressing the group so the plain register stays polite.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình for the singular "brother" (also 14:13, 14:15, 14:21)
decisions.reason: The brother is a fellow believer, man or woman (m2). Vietnamese does not mark number here, so the span the style guide sets for believers reads naturally of one person: "anh chị em mình" is one's fellow believer. Readable says "một tín hữu khác", as the English Readable says "a fellow believer".

decisions.choice: um irmão ou uma irmã na fé
decisions.reason: For "a fellow believer" in the English Readable (here and in verses 13, 15, 20 and 21). Portuguese has no common word for a fellow believer that is not masculine; "crente" in Brazil means an evangelical Protestant. "Um irmão ou uma irmã na fé" says plainly that men and women are meant, so no setting is needed.

source.text: ἢ καὶ σὺ τί ἐξουθενεῖς τὸν ἀδελφόν σου;

records.literal_gloss: Or also you, why despise you the brother of you?

en.L: Or you also, why do you look down on your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}?
en.B: Or you, why do you look down on your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}?
en.R: And you who eat anything, why do you look down on a fellow believer?

es.L: ¿O también tú, por qué desprecias a tu hermano?
es.B: ¿O tú, por qué miras con desprecio a tu hermano?
es.R: Y tú, que comes de todo, ¿por qué desprecias a otro creyente?
